analysis:
Examined all supplied excerpts of docs/provider/two-mac-cluster.md. Visible HEAD lines 1–455 match BASE: pairing confirmation, authenticated model transfer, manifest/build checks, coordinator approval expiry, local/public separation, media refusal and memory admission are unchanged. BASE lines 464–504 describe encrypted, tenant-scoped pair caches relevant to A-001/T-041; no changed cache behavior is visible. Existing local HTTP exposure and developer worker overrides are not new findings.
The bounded patch introduces default-on coordinated automatic updates at HEAD lines 536–543, replacing BASE lines 536–562's manual updates and service restart instructions. Each service now queries the coordinator on a pairing-derived slot and reportedly downloads, verifies and stages a release while serving. This changes the update lifecycle but the supplied HEAD excerpt ends at line 455 and the patch stops at the first update step, so it does not establish a missing control or a concrete regression.
Integration must inspect the remaining changed update documentation (HEAD 536–583, 644–645) and supplied updater implementation for authenticated release/artifact verification, matching rank identities, safe stop/restart and rollback, approval revalidation, and cache/model bindings across updates. These concern A-011/A-017, T-013/T-034/T-043 and T-053/T-054, plus serving availability A-018. BASE already replanned on worker changes; automatic installation must be distinguished from that existing behavior. Update verification and orchestration remain unverified contracts in this source scope, not proven vulnerabilities. No runtime implementation was supplied here.
